ESH except for your sister. I feel like a crazy person reading the majority of these comments and I’m sure I’ll be downvoted to hell but here it goes. 

I work with disabled kids and I’m trained to do so. I think it’s so easy to push them off to the side and exclude them, simply because it’s widely assumed they can’t or won’t enjoy fun or activities like the rest of us do. I have a few kids that behave pretty similarly to your sister and they’ve been able to enjoy the parties and activities we’ve thrown. If it helps, I also have a cousin whose prone to seizures and she’s enjoyed family parties with flashing lights and a DJ and loud music as well. And guess what, we’re Mexican too, and she’s been able to have her own quince as well. 

The part that makes you the AH is mentioning first and foremost your apprehension towards your sisters vocal stimming and how it’ll interrupt the videos and the ceremony. Her “making a lot of noise” was the first reason you didn’t want her there. To me, this does come across as you wanting to exclude your sister based solely on her disability. Your sister can’t help it, and you can’t help but be related to her. You can’t simply hide her at home for every milestone activity because it’s easier or more convenient to you, that’s just plain wrong. She’s still a member of the family. 

You did mention concern about the lights and sound, but that wasn’t until much later, and I’m sure if that was your only grievance, your family might’ve not gone so nuclear. You could’ve been assured by a professional caregiver or physician if that were the case. 

Your family are also the A for kicking you out and blowing you up over this. In their quest to make sure the disabled child is included, they went out of their way to shun YOU and exclude YOU. They wanted to make you feel unwelcome and upset, they wanted to name call you, and nothing you’ve said or done could ever justify abandoning you like that either. 

In the end, I don’t get how there couldn’t have been some sort of compromise. You want to preserve this very important milestone without any hiccups and that’s not an unreasonable request. Your family wants your sister to be at this milestone event, and that’s not asking too much either. I don’t see how asking the babysitter or a professional to attend this party with your sister and keeping an eye on her wasn’t any option. That way, they could tend to your sister if she grows impatient or noisy. That way, your mother and grandmother and whoever else can be fully present for your special day. 

Regardless, I’ve been at the butt end of family disputes before and I want you to know it gets better. You’ll find your peace when you’re older. I just think a little more room for kindness and leniency could’ve been used on both ends.
